messages:
sam: Quick kernel question — my H100 runs best with FlashAttention v3 for small-batch low-latency requests, but in us-west we saw Triton kernels beat it for long sequences. Need a pragmatic rulebook for when to switch kernels across regions/GPU types.

jia: Can you paste the perf numbers (seq len, batch, model, precision, p50/p95/throughput)?

sam: Pasted quick run from yesterday (13B chat, fp16 / q8 runs):
```
# region,gpu,kernel,seq,batch,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens/s
us-east,H100,flashv3,128,2,45,90,12000
us-east,H100,triton,128,2,60,110,9000
us-west,A100,flashv3,1024,16,220,480,15000
us-west,A100,triton,1024,16,190,360,18000
eu-west,A100,2048,32,520,980,17000
eu-west,H100,2048,32,600,1200,15000
# q8 note: flashv3 on H100 regressed ~10% throughput in q8 compared to fp16
```

frank: TL;DR — flashv3 wins for small seqs and latency-sensitive slices (p50), Triton wins for large seq+heavy batching (throughput) especially on A100. The q8 regression on H100 looks like a kernel codepath mismatch (we saw similar on an old CuBLAS upgrade).

jia: Agree. For routing rules: prefer FlashAttn v3 on H100 for seq <= 512 and batch <= 8 (low latency). Prefer Triton on A100 for seq >= 1024 or batch >= 16 (throughput). Use vendor libs/CUTLASS as fallback when quantized int kernels outperform both. :thumbsup:

lisa: Implementation notes — runtime should evaluate request.metadata.seq_len and .batch_size, then pick kernel variant. Example policy config: 
```
- name: kernel_policy_v1
  rules:
    - if: seq_len <= 512 and batch <= 8 and gpu_type == H100
      kernel: flashv3
    - if: seq_len >= 1024 and batch >= 16 and gpu_family == A100
      kernel: triton
    - else: kernel: runtime_heuristic
```
We also need a compatibility check (kernel supports quantization level, model dtype).

benchbot: Bench data uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/17725/flashv3_vs_triton_region_report.csv and a quick chart in Grafana dashboard "kernels/regional-comparison".

frank: Also call out build matrix — some CUDA/toolkit versions change relative wins. We should tag benchmark runs with driver/runtime versions and record kernel implementations (flash v2/v3 commit hashes, triton release).

sam: Proposed actionable decision:
- Default policy: seq <= 512 & batch <= 4 -> FlashAttn v3 on H100 (latency SLOs).
- Default policy: seq >= 1024 & batch >= 16 -> Triton on A100 (throughput SLOs).
- If quantized (q8/q4) run, consult perf tag: if vendor int kernels > 1.05x throughput -> prefer vendor.
- Fallback: runtime_heuristic that tries top-2 kernels w/ fast micro-bench and picks winner.
I'll open a PR with the config + telemetry hooks.

jia: sgtm. Add telemetry for p95, token_cost/token, and per-kernel failure rates. Also add a regression smoke test that runs q8 output drift checks between kernels to catch quality regressions.

lisa: Assigning tasks — sam = PR with config, frank = expanded bench matrix (drivers/toolkit), jia = perf dashboard + smoke tests. I'll schedule a canary rollout across us-east and eu-west next Tue.

sam: OK will start the PR today and include the micro-benchmark script. Thanks all. :rocket:
